title: Homes as Assets
sentences: A house performs two functions that are quietly incompatible.
It shelters a household and it stores accumulated wealth.
For decades those functions could be pursued without visible conflict.
Sustained price growth eventually made the second dominant.
A society that needs housing to be cheap cannot also need it to appreciate.
Most political arguments about housing avoid stating that plainly.
Existing owners are numerous, organised and understandably protective.
Those who need to buy are younger, dispersed and rarely decisive at elections.
The outcome follows from the arithmetic rather than from any conspiracy.
Nothing resolves until one of the two functions is openly given priority.
